rationale: No research design is recommended because no new study is proposed. The effectiveness of nurse-led titration on doses reached and hospitalisation is established by a randomised comparison (c1) and a systematic review of 11 studies (c2). What the service still needs to know is local: whether its patients reach target doses, whether four-class titration stays safe (c3) and whether access is equitable. That is answered by a registered service evaluation with pre-specified measures and a monthly review, not by a comparative study.
alternatives: Randomised comparison of nurse-led and consultant titration in this hospital (refused: repeats a settled question and delays treatment for the comparison group)
Before-after research study of doses reached with a formal hypothesis test (refused: adds analysis burden without changing the decision)
Keep titration in consultant clinics and add extra clinic slots (considered: fewer changes per year and no nurse capacity used)
guidelines: SQUIRE 2.0 for any written report of the service evaluation
whyNotMoreComplex: A local trial would need a comparison group kept on slower titration for months, which the retrieved evidence gives no reason to accept; monitoring with pre-specified measures answers the local questions.

decision.statement: Set up the nurse-led titration clinic as a routine service under the signed-off protocol and monitor it against pre-specified measures of doses reached, safety events and missed visits; do not run a new comparative study.
decision.question: Should the heart failure service set up a nurse-led titration clinic now, or study nurse-led titration first?

criteria.text: Nurse-led titration has increased the proportion of patients at target doses in a randomised comparison and in pooled studies.
Local safety events exceed those reported, with potassium above 6.0 mmol/L in more than 5 percent of titrated patients.

gates.requirement: Titration protocol signed off by the cardiology clinical lead
gates.evidence: Sign-off HF-TP-2026-03 dated 2026-09-08, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Monitoring plan registered with clinical governance as a service evaluation
gates.evidence: Registration SE-2026-044 dated 2026-09-15, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Both nurses registered as independent prescribers
gates.evidence: Non-medical prescribing policy NMP-04 register entries, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Extra consultant clinic slots for titration
Nurse-led titration for recently discharged patients only
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; all gates rest on investigator-supplied records.

summary: No new study: implement the clinic as a service with monitoring; the decision rests on three ledger claims and all gates are met.
